resources.string: Guard is watching your phone right now.
Turn on a feature below to start watching.
Guard keeps a quiet notice in your status bar. That notice is what lets it keep watching while your screen is off — swipe it away and the watching stops.
Get an alert the moment your phone is plugged in or unplugged.
Sound a loud alarm if someone picks your phone up or moves it.

Sound the alarm when you clap, so you can find your phone. The microphone only listens for the sound of a clap — nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere. Android shows a microphone dot in your status bar while this is on.
Paused. Android will not let Guard open the microphone by itself after a restart, so it waits until you open the app.
Not listening. Guard needs permission to use the microphone before it can hear a clap.
The quiet notice that keeps Guard watching.
Alerts for anything Guard spots on your phone.
The alarm is sounding. Tap to open Guard.
The alarm is sounding. Tap to open Guard.
Clap detection needs turning back on
Charger and motion protection restarted after your phone rebooted. Android does not let Guard open the microphone on its own, so open Guard to start listening for claps again.
Guard no longer has permission to use the microphone. Your other protection is unaffected. Open Guard to grant it again.
Anti-theft monitoring. Guard watches power state and device sensors while the owner is away and must keep running with the screen off to raise an alarm the moment the phone is disturbed.
